senses.sense: Skilled working that is set beside or against Nature: what is done by skill rather than grown or done of itself.

evidence.quote: naturally proceeding without art
because Art and Nature, like mother and daughter, consent to each other
Art imitateth Nature and supplyeth its defects
the greatest miracle of Nature wrought by Art
which cannot be prolong'd by any art or help of Man

senses.sense: A discipline of knowledge and practice, mostly named by its subject or work (fire and Chymistry, Physick, separating, distilling, the Magicall and Cabalisticall); also false arts that are sold.

evidence.quote: the Art of Fire and Chymistry
the Art of Phisick is so immense and large
who would not instruct every one in the Art of Physick
born to crush the truth of the Physicall Art
by reason of the out-cry against their uncertaine art
this Separatory art which teacheth rightly to discerne and seperate the Good from the Bad
if he had been well skild in the Distillatory Art
the whole Foundation of the Magicall and Cabalisticall Art
nor be certaine in his Art
the searchers out of difficult Arts
whose Nativity is not disposed to that Art by the Sears
sel their forged Cachochymicall and Sophisticall Arts

senses.sense: 'the Art' with no name added, in the defence of Alchymistry: the art that bad practisers abuse and lay open. Interpreted (this writer's inference): it is the Alchymistry the same passages speak of, from OPEN.11 beside N020 ('true and noble Alchymistry' made infamous) and CH5.54 (the vulgar Alchymists would prostitute the Art); the lines do not name it outright.

evidence.quote: These are not the vices of the Art, but of men abusing the Art
the most laudable and honourable name of true and noble Alchymistry, hath been unworthily made infamous and odious
those circumforanceous and vulgar Alchymists would have surpassed all other Physitians, and prostituted the Art

senses.sense: 'this Art' / 'the Art' in the chapter on the one chief Medicine: the art of preparing that Medicine, a secret the Phylosophers keep close. Interpreted (this writer's inference): CH6.4 joins 'the preparation hereof' with 'this Art', and the chapter's title names the chief Medicine.

evidence.quote: whether fot ostentation sake I ambitiously arrogate to my selfe the absolute knowledge of this Art
He that desireth this Art, must not be a slave to other mens judgment
worthy men, and sworn in this Art
keeping close the secret of the Art by a constant Taciturnity

senses.sense: A particular skilful means or device by which one thing is done (a trick of the hand, a means of cure, whatever means a man tries).

evidence.quote: he would by a singuler art pull it out againe by the poynt
cured by a wonderfull Art
let that man use what Arts soever he can

senses.sense: Art as Nature's own: the skill Nature has and rejoices in. Interpreted (this writer's inference) from the one note alone.

evidence.quote: rejoyceth in its master, and in its art and vertues

senses.sense: The 'arts' of the Elements, held in the Fift Essence. Interpreted (this writer's inference): their workings or actings, from N281 'the Naturall life is nothing else but the actings of the Elements'; the lines do not say more.

evidence.quote: in which are all the Elements actually, and all their arts
the Naturall life is nothing else but the actings of the Elements
